name: Ryumonji Zen Monastery
technique: Shikantaza (just sitting) zazen within a traditional Japanese Soto monastic form
teacherAccess: Resident Abbot Rev. Shoken Winecoff, a dharma heir of Dainin Katagiri Roshi trained at Zuioji Senmon Sodo in Japan, leads sesshin, gives dharma talks, and is available for dokusan during practice periods.
retreatOptions: Monthly weekend sesshin (arrive Friday evening, depart Sunday noon) plus traditional Winter and Summer Ango practice periods lasting several weeks for full- or part-time residential training.
about: Ryumonji is a Soto Zen Buddhist monastery on a 40-acre former farmstead in the rolling hills of northeast Iowa, formally registered as a temple with the Soto Zen Headquarters in Japan. Founded in 2000 by Rev. Shoken Winecoff, a disciple of Dainin Katagiri Roshi, the monastery has since built a Buddha Hall, entry gate, bell tower, and dedicated residential buildings (Kuin and Sodo/Shuryo) purpose-built for monastic training. Visitors join a living community for zazen, chanting, oryoki meals, and work practice under a traditional daily schedule. The monastery offers both accessible weekend sesshin for newcomers and longer immersive Ango practice periods for residential monastic training. All programs are offered on a dana (free-will donation) basis with dormitory-style housing provided on-site.
schedule: Weekend sesshin held roughly monthly year-round; Winter Ango runs January 20 to March 19 and Summer Ango runs June 16 to September 17 each year.
cost: No set fee for sesshin or ango; free-will dana offerings are customary.

pricePerDay.notes: Ryumonji charges no fees for sesshin or ango; participation is entirely dana (free-will donation) based with no suggested amount published.

foodNotes: Communal oryoki-style meals are taken in silence with the community; special dietary and medical needs can be accommodated with advance notice.
workNotes: Daily work periods (samu) are a formal, scheduled part of both sesshin and ango.
